title: Borrow + Contract: Safe Queue
story: A message broker silently dropped 10,000 messages because a consumer called dequeue on an empty queue inside a tight loop. The bug went unnoticed for weeks — contracts would have trapped instantly at the first violation.
why: Combining borrow semantics with contracts creates data structures that are both memory-safe AND logically correct.
analogy: Borrows are the lock on a door (mutual exclusion). Contracts are the sign on the door ('Occupancy limit: 50'). Both must be satisfied before you enter.
try_it: Add a `Queue.peek` method that takes `&Queue` (immutable borrow) and returns `Option[Int]`. Requires `items.len() > 0`. Now you can inspect the front element without dequeuing — the immutable borrow guarantees no one can dequeue behind your back.
tips: Use `&mut` for mutation operations, `&` for read-only queries — the borrow checker enforces this at compile time
Contracts on borrowed parameters prevent the caller from sneaking in invalid state under the borrow
The invariant on capacity prevents silent overflows — if you add capacity checks, make them an invariant
common_mistakes: Calling `dequeue` without checking if the queue is empty — use `q.items.len() > 0` or wrap in `is_full` logic
Using `&mut` on a query method — it prevents other code from reading the queue simultaneously
Forgetting that `enqueue` consumes capacity — if you enqueue 5 times on a capacity-5 queue, the 6th call traps
